finalText:
I've identified the keyword, value and a word-for-word quote for all ten topics. Every quote comes from the Revision 4 text at https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html.

**Which revision is current:** The page is titled "NIST SP 800-63B-4, Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management" and dated 26 Aug 2025. Its abstract says "This publication supersedes NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-63B." The 2017 Revision 3 is still online at https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html, but I didn't quote it. One gap: the CSRC landing page (https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/63/b/4/final) returned a 404 error. So I couldn't check NIST's official status page to rule out a later errata update or draft. My search turned up nothing newer than Revision 4.

**What Revision 4 says (sections 3.1.1.1 and 3.1.1.2):**
- **Minimum length:** Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require at least 15 characters for a password that is the only authentication factor. A password used only as part of multi-factor authentication MAY be shorter, but it SHALL still be at least eight characters.
- **Maximum length:** they SHOULD permit a maximum length of at least 64 characters.
- **Composition rules, periodic changes, hints and security questions:** all are SHALL NOT. For periodic changes, verifiers still SHALL force a change if there is evidence the password has been compromised.
- **Blocklist:** verifiers SHALL compare a new or changed password against a blocklist.
- **Password managers:** verifiers SHALL allow password managers and autofill. They SHOULD also permit "paste".
- **Storage:** passwords SHALL be salted and hashed, and the salt SHALL be at least 32 bits. Using an approved hashing scheme from the latest revision of SP 800-132 is only a SHOULD, not a SHALL.

The text on the page matched the plan's expected keywords for every topic, including SHOULD for the SP 800-132 hashing scheme.
